## Backing Query SQL

```sql
SELECT
  _stage_inner."orders.order_date" AS "order_date",
  _stage_inner."orders.rev" AS "rev"
FROM (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', orders.order_date) AS "orders.order_date",
    CAST(SUM(orders.amount) AS DOUBLE) AS "orders.rev"
  FROM orders AS orders
  GROUP BY
    DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', orders.order_date)
) AS _stage_inner
```

## Data Profile SQL

```sql
WITH monthly_rev AS (
  SELECT
    _stage_inner."orders.order_date" AS "order_date",
    _stage_inner."orders.rev" AS "rev"
  FROM (
    SELECT
      DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', orders.order_date) AS "orders.order_date",
      CAST(SUM(orders.amount) AS DOUBLE) AS "orders.rev"
    FROM orders AS orders
    GROUP BY
      DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', orders.order_date)
  ) AS _stage_inner
)
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS "monthly_rev._count",
  COUNT(DISTINCT monthly_rev.order_date) AS "monthly_rev.order_date_count_distinct",
  CAST(AVG(monthly_rev.rev) AS DOUBLE) AS "monthly_rev.rev_avg"
FROM monthly_rev AS monthly_rev
LIMIT 3
```

args.message: I can't break January 2025 down by day using monthly_rev. That model is already summed to one row per month: it groups order_date to the first of the month and totals the amounts into rev. The daily detail isn't stored there, and when I tried to query it by day, SLayer refused because the column is already at month level. A daily breakdown would have to come from the underlying orders model (sum of amount by order_date per day), which wouldn't be the monthly_rev summary you asked for.
